programme: A two-part axis rather than one complex: SKI, acting through SMAD7-linked TGF-β modulation, drives medullary thymic epithelial cell (mTEC) differentiation and thereby sets the central-tolerance checkpoint that determines which T cells are deleted before export; NFKB1 is the canonical downstream effector that, once autoreactive T cells escape that checkpoint, drives the inflammatory target programme (TNF, IL6, IFNG, CCL5, ICAM1, VCAM1, BIRC3, CSF1) responsible for peripheral autoimmune tissue damage.
role_in_a: In Multiple Sclerosis, NFKB1 sits at the centre of the documented neuroinflammatory programme: retrieved work ties it to microglial activation, demyelinating lesion biology, and biomarker/diagnostic models for the disease (PMID 40327306, 41420758, 39855613, 35287559), consistent with its very large, canonical inflammatory target set (TNF, IL6, IFNG, ICAM1, VCAM1, CCL5) and its recorded Open Targets association (percentile 0.586).
role_in_b: In Thymoma, SKI is directly shown to regulate mTEC differentiation and, through that, peripheral T cell output (PMID 38767415) — the mechanism by which a thymic epithelial tumour disrupts central deletion of self-reactive T cells. NFKB1 independently carries a comparatively high Open Targets association in Thymoma (percentile 0.904) and observed ReMap binding, consistent with NF-κB pathway activity in thymic epithelial tumour biology, though no retrieved paper states this explicitly.
shared_axis: A thymic epithelial tumour that perturbs SKI-dependent mTEC differentiation would degrade central tolerance and release autoreactive T cell clones into the periphery; those clones, once activated, would signal through the same NFKB1-driven inflammatory programme that is independently documented as central to MS demyelinating pathology. The pairing is a tolerance-failure-to-inflammation logic, not a shared cell type or shared literature.
reasoning: Each half of the axis is independently anchored in the record — SKI in a mechanistically specific thymic-epithelial-tolerance paper, NFKB1 in several MS-specific papers plus placement in both Open Targets sets — so the module is nameable and each factor is placed in at least one disease. But nothing retrieved connects the two diseases through this axis directly; the bridge (central tolerance failure → peripheral NFKB1-driven autoimmunity) is inferred, not documented for this pair, which caps this at moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 38767415 shows SKI regulates medullary thymic epithelial cell differentiation and controls peripheral T cell response; PMID 40327306 links NFKB1-associated genes to a multiple sclerosis complication (neuropathic bladder) via susceptibility-gene analysis; PMID 41420758 examines a neuroprotective compound against demyelination with NFKB1 pathway relevance; PMID 39855613 builds an MS diagnostic model from lipid-metabolism genes including NFKB1; PMID 35287559 shows an anti-inflammatory compound protecting against EAE (an MS model) via microglial NF-κB inhibition.
how_to_falsify: In an mTEC or thymic organoid model, knock down SKI and test whether central deletion of self-reactive T cell clones is unaffected (no change in autoreactive T cell export) — if tolerance is intact despite SKI loss, the thymic-tolerance half of the axis fails. Separately, profile NFKB1 target-gene activity (TNF, IL6, ICAM1, VCAM1) in MS lesion tissue or PBMCs against matched controls; if these are not elevated, the peripheral-inflammation half fails, and the proposed bridge between the two diseases has no support.
caveats: Only 2 of the 12 concordant factors (SKI, NFKB1) carry this account; HOXA2, OSR1, SIX4, KAT6B, RUNX2, ONECUT1 and HEYL are developmental/differentiation TFs with no disease-specific evidence in either direction and are treated here as background rather than mechanism. NAB2, KLF7 and HMGB2 each have only single-disease-adjacent evidence (solitary fibrous tumour biology for NAB2, a biomarker mention for KLF7, tangential cancer/innate-immunity papers for HMGB2, including one paper nominally covering both diseases but only via a generic ribosome-biogenesis/innate-immunity link) and were left out of the carrying set as too thin to anchor a claim. Support fractions for the carrying factors are 91–94/260 (~35%), a recurring but minority pattern, drawn from only 3 independent cohort pairs. FOXN1 and IRF5 — the more obvious thymic-epithelial and MS-autoimmune master regulators — appear only in the single-view exclusion list and must not be substituted into this account. Brain and thymus are anatomically unrelated tissues, and MS is not the classical thymoma-associated paraneoplastic autoimmune disease (myasthenia gravis is); this account is a general tolerance-failure logic, not a documented clinical association.
